newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise again; Dow within record range.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise again; Dow within record range.

text.p: Stocks rose for the third straight day Wednesday after a report of surprisingly strong economic growth in a broad rally that carried the Dow above 7,000 for the first time in seven weeks.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 46.96 points to close at 7,008.99, a day after soaring 179 points in its second largest point gain ever. The index is within reach of its March 11 record close of 7,085.16.
In the broader market, advancing issues outnumbered declines 1,599 to 942 on heavy volume of 556 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The market extended a rebound that has seen the Dow recapture more than 600 of the 700 points it lost between March 11 and April 11. That sell-off was fuelled by worries about the impact on the economy and corporate profits of an interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve.
The central bank raised a key short-term rate a quarter point on March 25, and hinted it would again raise rates to slow the economy and head off inflationary pressures.
The market's rise on Wednesday came despite a report of much-stronger-than expected first quarter economic growth.

The Commerce Department reported the nation's gross domestic product expanded at a 5.6 percent annual rate in the quarter, its fastest pace in more than nine years. The GDP number was much stronger than Wall Street economists' forecasts for a 4.1 percent rate of growth.

If new economic data affirms the belief that growth is moderating and inflation is under control, the market may well set new highs as investors skake off worries of further rate increases by the Fed.
But some analysts were reluctant to declare the market's correction at an end, at least until stocks find their way back into record ground. Even so, the pace of the rebound was surprising.

"This market truly has been manic-depressive in the last six weeks," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We corrected in four weeks and rallied almost all the way back in about two."
If rates are in fact headed higher, the recent bounce may be close to its conclusion, some analysts said.
"It's certainly difficult to expect the market to make much headway here with a rate increase still on the table," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp.

Another economic statistic will keep stock traders on the edge of their seats on Thursday. The highlight will be the National Association of Purchasing Management's manufacturing index for April, which is expected to fall to 53.6 from 55.0 in March, according to a Reuters poll.
The April jobs report due on Friday is among those the Fed watches closely in gauging inflation pressures. As a result, few on Wall Street are modifying their interest rate outlooks yet.
"We remain convinced the Fed will tighten some more," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "Nothing we've seen changes that opinion."
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury rose 10/32, sending its yield down to 6.96 percent from Tuesday's 6.98 percent. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.
Retailers and other cyclical issues turned in a solid performance, boosted by the robust economic picture. Woolworth Corp. gained 1-3/8 to 21-1/2 and Dayton Hudson Corp. rose 2-1/2 to 45.

Technology stocks were also strong, led by a resurgent networking group. Ascend Communications Corp. surged 4-5/16 to 45-3/4, Bay Networks Inc. gained 1-1/2 to 17-7/8 and Cisco Systems Inc. rose 1-3/4 to 51-3/4.
Sinter Metals Inc. soared 9-35/64 to 36-35/64 after Britain's GKN Plc offered to buy the auto parts maker for $37 a share, or $570 million.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 18.13 points to 1,260.76.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 7.29 points to 801.34. The American Stock Exchange index rose 4.88 to 552.91.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.32 to 416.94. The average share was up 33 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,519.287 up 69.824 or 0.94 percent.
